en.title: Powder alert for Alpe d'Huez? 18–62 cm of fresh snow next week (23–29 November)
en.description: Alpe d'Huez forecast for 23–29 November: 40 cm at the top, 35 cm mid-mountain. Wednesday 25 is the key day. Data from 16 November.
en.lede: Wednesday 25 November brings the heaviest snow to Alpe d'Huez for the week ahead. The top of the resort around 3200 m will collect 40 cm across the full week of 23–29 November (ranging from 18 to 62 cm), while mid-mountain sees 35 cm and the base 10 cm.

p: Most of next week's snow falls in four bursts. Tuesday 24 November brings 4 cm (high case 7 cm) at the top, followed by the main event on Wednesday 25 with 11 cm (up to 12 cm). Thursday 26 adds another 11 cm (reaching 17 cm in the high case), and Sunday 29 delivers 10 cm more (up to 20 cm). These are the figures at the top around 3200 m.
The timing matters more than perfect accuracy a week out. Wednesday morning, once the pistes are ready, is likely to be the best day to ski the fresh snow.

The gap between the top and base is sharp: 40 cm at the top against only 10 cm at the base tells you the snow line sits high through most of the week. Mid-mountain around 2200 m splits the difference at 35 cm (ranging 15 to 55 cm across the forecast uncertainty).
This steep height gradient means the lower pistes will see more rain than snow. Real snow cover for skiing builds only above mid-mountain.

sections.h: Where to find the best snow
p: Pic Blanc and the Sarenne glacier hold snow longest on this south-facing mountain. Aim for the Pic Blanc and Sarenne side early in the week before the sun begins to work on the big south-facing bowl.
Treat the lower terrain at Vaujany, Oz and Auris as the weak point for fresh snow. The base gets little accumulation, so these edges of the domain will thin quickly as the sun and wind do their work.

Next week does not start from bare ground. From 17 to 20 November the top is forecast to receive 78 cm (52–103 cm), a substantial fall that will be in place before Wednesday 25 arrives. By then, the upper mountain should already carry meaningful depth.
This two-step pattern—heavy snow earlier this week, then more next week—means early November visitors benefit from established cover, while late November skiers arrive to fresh snow on top of a base.

La Grave, 18 km away, is forecast to gather 49 cm at the top for the same week, edging out Alpe d'Huez's 40 cm. Les 2 Alpes (13 km) and Serre Chevalier (42 km) both forecast 47 cm. If you have flexibility and are chasing powder, La Grave has the edge.
The range of uncertainty is wide at all resorts: 18–62 cm for Alpe d'Huez means the low case is half the high case. Watch the forecast sharpen over the weekend before you book.

sections.h: What to pack for the base
p: The 10 cm at the base hides substantial rain. The village sits at 1124 m, well below where snow takes hold. Bring waterproof outer layers even though the top receives powder.

The resort is known for its sunny aspect, which is lovely later in the season but harsh on fresh snow in November. Wednesday and Thursday mornings, before the sun reaches the snowfields, give the longest-lived conditions.

advice: Off-piste: new snow creates new avalanche risk. Consult the French avalanche bulletin (BERA) for the massif before you venture beyond the marked runs.
Check the resort's lift status and opening date. Snow on the mountain does not guarantee lifts are running early in the season.
Plan for wet weather at the base. Pack rain gear and expect damp conditions in the village while the high peaks receive snow.
Aim for Wednesday 25 or Thursday 26 to ski the freshest snow at the top. Plan your visit around those days if possible.
Book with flexibility if you can. The forecast picture will be much sharper by the weekend; the total is uncertain, but the mid-week timing is reliable.
